answer: Stake-proportional reward shares. An island monitoring pool covering yarrow plots and falcon habitats can allocate its fixed budget in proportion to coins locked for the entire epoch. The verifier counts each locked coin once, regardless of the owner's account count. Splitting one stake among N identities leaves their combined share unchanged; increasing that share requires more immobilized capital and its opportunity cost. This assumes linear shares with no per-account bonus or minimum payout; either exception can reward splitting.
